title: Travel and accommodation
subtitle: scheduled flight, self-catering, rough it
summary: Book and describe any kind of trip - flights, cruises, trains and hire cars - and choose the right words for where you stay and how you spend the time.

lesson.heading: Booking a flight
lesson.text: A **scheduled flight** is a normal, regular flight; a **charter flight** is a special flight taking a group of people, usually to the same holiday destination. Cheap tickets often carry **restrictions** - you can only travel on certain days - and may be **non-refundable**, so you cannot get your money back, or carry a **cancellation fee**.

examples.text: It was a cheap fare, but there were some **restrictions**.
The ticket is relatively cheap, but it's **non-refundable**.
The ticket allowed us a three-night **stopover** in Singapore on the journey from London to Sydney.
examples.note: a stopover = a night somewhere before continuing to your destination

lesson.heading: Choices when you book
rows: how much comfort you pay for
the way you go, for example via Amsterdam
a low-cost or budget airline, or a national carrier
includes flight, accommodation and all meals, drinks and snacks in the hotel
airport taxes, insurance and similar additional costs
the coach or shuttle bus to and from your hotel

lesson.heading: Sea travel
lesson.text: Sea travel is normally on a **ferry**, and the journey is called a **crossing** - but a holiday on the sea is a **cruise**. For some people a luxury cruise is **the holiday of a lifetime**, one they will always remember. You can book a **berth** in a shared **cabin**, or pay more for a **deluxe** cabin on the **upper deck**.

examples.text: You can get a four-**berth** cabin on the ferry.
Cruises often go to **exotic** islands where you can **get away from it all**.
examples.note: exotic = unusual or exciting; get away from it all = escape your daily routine

left.label: Train travel
left.text: You relax and look at the countryside through the windows of your **carriage**. Railways link major towns, but you may have to **change trains** if you cannot get a **through train**.
examples: Our seats were in the first **carriage**.
It's a **through train** - you don't have to change at Crewe.

right.label: Car hire
right.text: **Car hire** is another way of **getting around** (informal). You may have to choose whether you want **unlimited mileage**, and there may be **extras** such as accident insurance.
examples: With **unlimited mileage** you can travel as many miles as you like for the same price.
If you hire a car, it gives you the freedom to **come and go as you please**.

lesson.heading: Accommodation when travelling
rows: sleeping in a tent or a caravan
accommodation where you do your own cooking
a small cottage or cabin specially built for holiday-makers
similar to a pub but also offering accommodation, often in an attractive old building
usually breakfast and one other meal

lesson.heading: Talking about the holiday itself
rows: to live in very basic conditions, without extra comforts
to sleep out in the open, with no roof over your head
to be out in the wilds
to be far away from civilisation
to sit or lie and relax for long periods
to go along with the pace of things, with no fixed plan
to travel from place to place rather than stay put

lesson.text: A package holiday covers flight, hotel and transfers; an all-inclusive one adds every meal and drink as well.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with the word it goes with.
It was a regular flight which the airline runs every day - a ___ flight.
exercises.explanation: A scheduled flight is a normal, regular flight.

exercises.prompt: I hate ___ flights where everyone on board is booked to the same holiday destination.
exercises.explanation: A charter flight is a special flight taking a group of people, usually to the same holiday destination.

exercises.prompt: The ticket allowed us a three-night ___ in Singapore on the journey from London to Sydney.
exercises.explanation: A stopover lets you stay somewhere overnight before continuing to your destination.

exercises.prompt: It was a cheap fare, but there were some ___ - we could only travel midweek.
exercises.explanation: Restrictions limit when or how you can use a cheap ticket.

exercises.prompt: The ticket is relatively cheap, but it's ___ if you have to cancel.
exercises.explanation: A non-refundable ticket means you cannot get your money back.

exercises.prompt: The price includes the flight, the hotel and all your food and drink - it's an ___ holiday.
exercises.explanation: An all-inclusive holiday includes flight, accommodation and all meals, drinks and snacks.

exercises.prompt: The bus or taxi to your hotel is included in the cost of the holiday. What are they called?
exercises.explanation: Transfers are the coach or shuttle bus to and from your hotel.

exercises.prompt: Which word describes a small, relatively cheap hotel?
exercises.explanation: A guest house is a small, relatively cheap hotel; an inn is like a pub with rooms; a chalet is a holiday cottage.

exercises.prompt: It was a lovely cruise; we just ___ around all day.
exercises.explanation: To lounge around is to sit or lie and relax for long periods.

exercises.prompt: I prefer self-catering because I like to be my own ___.
exercises.explanation: To be your own boss is to decide everything for yourself.

exercises.prompt: Camping is OK if you don't mind ___ it - no hot water, no comfortable bed.
exercises.explanation: To rough it is to live in very basic conditions, without any extra comforts.

exercises.prompt: I'd hate to stay in just one place on my holiday - I much prefer to keep on the ___.
exercises.explanation: To keep on the move is to travel from place to place rather than stay put.

exercises.statement: Half board usually means breakfast and one other meal.
exercises.explanation: Correct - full board means all meals.

exercises.prompt: Which holiday does each expression go with?

items.text: to be out in the wilds
to spend a fortune on entrance fees

exercises.prompt: Put this sentence about hiring a car in order.
exercises.answer: If you hire a car, you can come and go as you please
exercises.explanation: To come and go as you please is to go where you want, when you want.
